c61_pro_thinking_005.label: Distributional Hypothesis of Meaning
c61_pro_thinking_005.description: The distributional hypothesis states that words with similar meanings occur in similar contexts; a word's meaning can be inferred from the company it keeps.
coverage_criteria: State the distributional hypothesis.
Given example sentences, identify words that are likely semantically related based on shared contexts.
Explain why 'hot' and 'cold' might be considered similar under this hypothesis despite being antonyms.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source introduces the Distributional Hypothesis with a clear example (cold/warm/hot/cool and yesterday/today/tomorrow/Tuesday) and states that words with similar distributions have similar meanings.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a fundamental theoretical concept that underpins all count-based and predictive word vector methods; it is a single claim that can be tested by having students identify context-based relationships.
